rca.root_cause: Commit 2f5bdb08 added a duplicate-payment probe query that is timing out on PostgreSQL, causing all POST /payments requests to exceed the timeout threshold. The trace shows 5046.1ms (98.3%) spent in PostgreSQL during a 5132.44ms total request, indicating a blocking database operation.
causal_chain: duplicate-payment probe query executes against PostgreSQL
PostgreSQL query takes 5046.1ms, likely due to unoptimized query or missing index
request exceeds timeout threshold at 5132.44ms total
TimeoutError raised and logged as unhandled exception

alternative_hypotheses.hypothesis: PostgreSQL connection pool is exhausted or misconfigured, causing new connections to stall
alternative_hypotheses.why_less_likely: The trace shows a successful connect span and only one logical operation (the probe query). Pool exhaustion would typically show multiple queued connections, not a single long-running query.

alternative_hypotheses.hypothesis: Network latency between payment-service and PostgreSQL increased independently
alternative_hypotheses.why_less_likely: The incident correlates directly with commit 2f5bdb08 deployed 2 hours before the incident. Network degradation would be independent of code changes and would affect other services similarly.

alternative_hypotheses.hypothesis: Fraud check downstream operation is hanging
alternative_hypotheses.why_less_likely: The trace shows postgresql consuming 98.3% of the time, and the duplicate-payment probe is executed *before* the fraud check according to the commit message, so the probe query is the bottleneck.

rca.recommended_action: Immediately revert commit 2f5bdb08 to restore service availability. Post-incident, analyze the duplicate-payment probe query: add appropriate indexes, optimize the WHERE clause, or implement pagination/caching to prevent full table scans that cause the 5-second latency.
unknowns: The exact SQL query in the duplicate-payment probe and whether it has an index on the queried columns
Whether the PostgreSQL server has resource constraints (CPU, memory) or slow query logging enabled
Why the probe query was not performance-tested before deployment
